title: About RacketWiki
lead: RacketWiki is a reference for every racket sport: the rules, equipment, courts, brands, players, competitions and the organisations that run each game, with every fact traced to its source.

children.text: We cover the well-known sports and the obscure ones in the same structure, so you can compare a padel court with a squash court, or a badminton racket with a table tennis bat, on one page.
How we work
Every fact that could be wrong carries a source, the tier of that source and the date we last checked it. Where we do not know something yet, the page says so instead of guessing.
Our summaries are written by our editors from the primary sources, which we link to. We do not copy text from other websites.
Sponsorship

RacketWiki is sponsored by Rallio, a club app for mixers, ladders, competitions and box leagues. Sponsored placements are always labelled, and sponsorship never changes what we publish or how the directory is ordered.
Get involved
If you spot a mistake, every page has a link to tell us. Clubs, coaches, retailers and makers can submit a directory listing, which an editor checks before it appears.

seo.title: About RacketWiki
seo.description: RacketWiki is a sourced reference for every racket sport: rules, equipment, courts, brands, players, competitions and governing bodies.

title: Editorial standards
lead: Every rule, measurement and ranking on RacketWiki comes from a source, listed at the foot of each page. Sources are ranked in five tiers, and a higher tier wins when two sources disagree.

children.text: The five tiers
Tier 1: governing bodies and official rulebooks.
Tier 2: national bodies, tours and tournament organisers.
Tier 3: manufacturers and recognised equipment test labs.
Tier 4: statistics and records bodies.
Tier 5: reputable press and community sources.
Our rules
Rules, court dimensions and equipment limits cite a Tier 1 source.
Rankings are always dated and cite the body that publishes them.
Encyclopaedias, including Wikipedia, can point us to a primary source but are never the citation.
Each page lists its sources at the foot and shows when its facts were last checked. Facts we have not yet verified are marked as such and never presented as fact.
Measurements are stored in metric and converted to imperial automatically, so the two never disagree.
Corrections
Every page has a "Spotted a mistake" link. Reports go to an editor, who checks them against the source before anything changes.
Sponsorship and the directory
Sponsored placements and sponsored directory listings are labelled "Sponsored" and their links are marked as sponsored. Directory order never depends on payment.
Influence

Sports, competitions, governing bodies and brands carry an influence rating from one to five rackets. It reflects how widely each one is played, followed and organised across racket sports. It is an editorial assessment rather than a sourced fact, and our editors review it. We use it to order lists, so the sports most people play come first.
